When a vendor’s invoice is received, it can be entered through either the Materials and Management Module (MM) or the Financial Accounting 
Module (FI). However, invoices should not be entered FI unless there is no corresponding PO or GR.  Invoices must be entered through MM for matching of the PO, GR and Invoice. Invoice Verification in Materials Management serves the following purpose: It completes the materials procurement, it allows invoices that do not originate in materials procurement (e.g. services, expenses, course costs, etc.) to be processed And it allows credit memos to be processed, either as invoice cancellations or discounts.

Different types of invoice verification exist: Purchase Order Based (All the items of a PO can be settled together, regardless of whether an item has been received in several partial deliveries. All the deliveries are totaled and posted as one item), Goods Receipt Based: (Each individual goods receipt is invoiced separately), Invoice without reference (When there is no reference to a PO, it is possible to post the transaction directly to a material account, a G/L account or an asset account), Evaluated Receipts Settlement (ERS) (The “invoice” is replaced by ERS - updates that would have occurred when the invoice was processed now takes place when the GR is processed)

Posting invoices via MM results in:  debit to GR/IR is the quantity received multiplied by the purchase order price, price differences between the PO and the invoice are recorded in a separate account configured for the invoice verification process, usually cash discounts or some similar account. Ideally, in the GR/IR account the debit from the invoice posting should exactly offset the credit from the receipt posting.

Posting invoices (especially the release of blocked invoices) is an important control point in the purchasing cycle. Posting invoices is one element in the 3-way matching between purchase order, goods receipt and invoice. The access to posting invoices and releasing blocked invoices must thus be well controlled.

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to Invoice posting functionality can lead to incorrect of unjustified payments of invoices and increases fraud vulnerability.

Module (FI). However, invoices should not be entered FI unless there is no corresponding PO or GR.  Invoices must be entered through MM for matching of the PO, GR and Invoice. Invoice Verification in Materials Management serves the following purpose: It completes the materials procurement, it allows invoices that do not originate in materials procurement (e.g. services, expenses, course costs, etc.) to be processed And it allows credit memos to be processed, either as invoice cancellations or discounts.

Different types of invoice verification exist: Purchase Order Based (All the items of a PO can be settled together, regardless of whether an item has been received in several partial deliveries. All the deliveries are totaled and posted as one item), Goods Receipt Based: (Each individual goods receipt is invoiced separately), Invoice without reference (When there is no reference to a PO, it is possible to post the transaction directly to a material account, a G/L account or an asset account), Evaluated Receipts Settlement (ERS) (The “invoice” is replaced by ERS - updates that would have occurred when the invoice was processed now takes place when the GR is processed)

Posting invoices via MM results in:  debit to GR/IR is the quantity received multiplied by the purchase order price, price differences between the PO and the invoice are recorded in a separate account configured for the invoice verification process, usually cash discounts or some similar account. Ideally, in the GR/IR account the debit from the invoice posting should exactly offset the credit from the receipt posting.

Posting invoices (especially the release of blocked invoices) is an important control point in the purchasing cycle. Posting invoices is one element in the 3-way matching between purchase order, goods receipt and invoice. The access to posting invoices and releasing blocked invoices must thus be well controlled.

Purchasing info records represent the relationship between a specific material or service and a vendor supplying the material or the service. 

There are two types of info record:
- info records with a material master record (e.g. for stock material).  This type of info record represents the relationship between a material or service (for which a master record exists) and a vendor.
- info records without a material master record (e.g. for consumable materials).  This type of info record represents the relationship between a material or service for which no master record exists and a vendor.

Purchase info records provide the purchasing department with valuable information like general data (e.g. reminders, units of measure), purchasing organization data (e.g. planned delivery time, delivery tolerance limits), pricing conditions (validity period, net price simulations), consignment price information (for vendor consignment material), Order price history (e.g. net price, price variance), Statistics (e.g. quantities and values, number of purchasing documents, delivery statistics) and Texts (e.g. info record texts – internal memo, purchase order text)

Maintenance of purchasing info records can be automated or manual. If the automatic option is chosen, the system ensures the maintenance of the records – e.g. the record points to the most recent purchasing document to determine the price used on a new purchasing document. In case the update is manual, the user must maintain the purchase info record on an on-going basis – e.g. in the current price changes, the user must update the purchasing info record to reflect the new price.

Thus, the info record allows buyers to quickly determine: which materials have been previously offered or supplied by a specific vendor, which vendors have offered or supplied a specific material, which quotation were received and so on. 

Other efficiency gains in the proper use of purchasing info record may be e.g. storage of current and future quotation conditions (discounts, fixed costs etc.) in the info record, in order to be able to copy them into PO’s.

Because info records are a key source of information for the purchasing and subsequent logistics processes, incorrect and/or unauthorized info record data can lead to incorrect purchase orders (wrong price, wrong vendor, wrong terms) and can seriously impact the logistics chain and consequently also the financial result of the organization.

description: MM-PUR: Maintain Contracts, Outline and Scheduling Agreements
riskText:
Contracts and Scheduling agreements are two variant of Outline Agreements and are important pieces of Master data in the Requisition to Pay process.
A (quantity) contract is an agreement that a supplier to order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities.  The supplier fulfills a contract by placing purchase orders against it. These purchase orders are known as release orders (or call-offs).  A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the requested quantities in the contract.
Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the supplier relationships when requisition schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of preferred customer status with suppliers which may lead to price increases.

Organizations must carry out a physical inventory of their warehouse stocks at least once per fiscal year to balance its inventory. To meet this legal requirement, various procedures and techniques can be implemented. The SAP System supports the following physical inventory procedures: periodic inventory, continuous inventory, cycle counting and inventory sampling

In the SAP System, physical inventory can be carried out both for a company's own stock and for special stock. Inventory for a company's stock and for special stocks (e.g, consignment stock at customer, external consignment stock from vendor or returnable packaging) must be taken separately (in different physical inventory documents).
Furthermore, the stock can be divided into stock types. In the standard system, a physical inventory can be carried out for the following stock types: unrestricted-use stock in the warehouse, stock in quality inspection and blocked stock

Inventory of all stock types mentioned can be taken in a single transaction. For the materials to be inventoried, one item is created in the physical inventory document for every stock type. Physical inventory takes place at storage location level. A separate physical inventory document is created for every storage location. Please note that the post of physical inventory differences also creates goods movements: Goods receipts for increases in stock levels and Goods issues for decreases in stock levels

As physical inventory relates to tangible goods that can be more or less vulnerable to theft, it is key that the different steps in the process are properly separated – basically the access to the physical goods and the record in the system containing information should be properly restricted and segregated.

Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to physical inventory functionality can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. It also makes organizations more vulnerable to theft and fraud.

description: MM-PUR: Release Purchase Requisitions with Classification
riskText:
Purchase requisitions are internal request to purchasing where an employee ask the buyer to provide a certain quantity of a material or service on a certain date.
Purchase requisition can be entered manually or through MRP.  The MRP controller can also convert a planned order into a purchase requisition. Source determination is a separate function.  The buyer immediately receives proposals if, e.g. fixed vendors or outline agreements exist for the material.

An electronic approval (release) procedure for purchase requisitions can be implemented.  According to certain conditions, the release procedure can determine that a purchase requisition item can only be approved for an RFQ or purchase order if it is released in sequence by certain persons or departments.
Purchase requisitions are optional - it is possible for buyers to raise purchase orders directly without referencing a requisition.  It is therefore important the release strategies (electronic approvals) also apply at the PO stage.

Important field in the Purchase requisition are: Goods Received and Invoice Received requirements for three way matching may be editable during purchase requisition or order entry. Matching criteria can be set to: “GR”: requiring receipt of goods before any payment processing, “IR”: requiring receipt of invoice before any payment processing; ”GR non-val”: stock is not valuated at time of receipt and is managed by quantity only (no financial accounting recognition is given to goods receipts and this setting turns off the use of the GR/IR account), “GR-based IR”: allows the matching of invoices to individual goods receipts in the case of partial shipments against a PO.  Use this option if a separate invoice is received for each good receipt.  With this setting, a GR must occur before an invoice can be entered. If the GR flag is not suppressed or display only it allows normal matching controls to be bypassed. Similarly, the GR non-val flag should also not be available under normal circumstances.  If business requirements exist for use of this flag it is recommended to defined this at the material master level, with no capability to override during requisitioning.

Release procedures can be implemented to enforce electronic approval of requisitions prior to further processing. Release Strategies include delegation levels and approval sequences based on various characteristics of the requisition like the Release Condition (The conditions for the release of a requisition item may be based on one or a combination of these factors: account assignment category, material group, plant, and the total value), Release Strategy (defines the approval process for requisitions. It defines who must approve a requisition and in what order it is to be approved)

Unauthorized or inappropriate access to Purchase Requisitions and Release procedures makes organizations more vulnerable to fraud by employees as configurable controls could be circumvented.

The source list is used in the administration of sources of supply. It specifies the allowed (and disallowed) sources of a material for a certain plant within a predefined period. It indicates the periods during with procurement from sources such as a vendor, an internal plant and an outline agreement are possible. A source list can be maintained manually or via mass changes via the use of the generate function which then reads existing valid purchasing scheduling agreements and purchase info records. To do so, the purchasing view of the material master must be configured to support this generate function.

The source list specifies the validity period, Fixed Vendor (e.g. preferred vendor), outline agreement (contract or scheduling), Blocked Vendor, Usage of MRP regarding vendor (MRP controller)

The MRP controller field has following functions: “ “ – MRP does not read the Source List when processing, “1” – MRP automatically pre-calculates Purchasing Requisitions with the identified contract or scheduling agreement number, “2” – MRP automatically maintains the Delivery Schedules for the identified Purchasing Scheduling agreement.

So basically, the source list serves:
- To define a source of supply as "fixed".
- To define a source of supply as "blocked".
- As an aid in selecting the preferred source during the source determination process.
- To block the external procurement of a material.

Stock transfers may also be referenced to a stock transport order.  The receiving plant would request a material using a stock transport order (similar to a purchase order).  The supplying plant would enter a transfer posting to move the stock from unrestricted-use to the receiving plant’s stock-in-transit.  The receiving plant receives the goods just as they would if they received goods from a vendor referencing the stock transport order instead of a PO.

The transfer of stock using a stock transport order has the following advantages compared with the transfer of stock without a stock transport order:  A goods receipt can be planned in the receiving plant, a vendor (transport vendor) can be entered in the stock transport order, delivery costs can be entered in the stock transport order, stock transport order is included in MRP and Purchase requisitions that were created in MRP can be converted into stock transport orders, the goods receipt can be posted directly to consumption and the entire process can be monitored via the purchase order history.

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to transport order functionality can lead to supply breaks, lost goods (property as goods are owned by the organization) and increases fraud vulnerability.

Inventory valuation in the SAP system uses various structures like the Valuation Area that specifies the level at which valuation is organized.  This may be specified as plant or company code.

The Valuation Class contains materials with similar properties that have been grouped together for accounting purposes so that they do not have to kept as separate stock accounts for every material. Which valuation class a material can be assigned to depends on the material type. Assignments can be defined in Customizing in 3 ways: All materials with the same material type are assigned to just one valuation class, Different materials with the same material type are assigned to different valuation classes, Materials with different material types are assigned to the one valuation class

A material is assigned to a valuation class in the material master record. The system checks whether the material type allows the material to be assigned to the valuation class specified.  The system refers to the valuation class of a material to determine which stock account to post to when a posting is made for this material.

The Valuation Category specifies the criterion according to which split valuation is to be carried out. E.g. Procurement (manufactured in-house or procured externally), Origin (domestic or abroad), Status (new, used, repaired)

Valuation categories are defined in Customization. A material is assigned a valuation category in the material master record.

The Valuation Type specifies the characteristic used for split valuation. The individual characteristics that make up a valuation category are called valuation types. For example, the valuation types in the valuation category Procurement are: internal and external. Valuation types are defined in Customizing. For every material with split valuation, you must enter all the valuation types allowed in the material master record.

Unauthorized and/or unqualified access to inventory valuation functionality can jeopardize the integrity of the inventory records and stock data (quantities and values) and of the production cycle. It also makes organizations more vulnerable to theft and fraud.

Contracts and Scheduling agreements are two variant of Outline Agreements and are important pieces of Master data in the Order to Cash process.
A (quantity) contract is an agreement that a customer will order a certain quantity of a product during a specified period. The contract contains basic quantity and price information but no schedule of specific delivery dates and quantities.  The customer fulfills a contract by placing sales orders against it. These sales orders are known as release orders (or call-offs).  A release order refers to the relevant contract and the system automatically updates the released quantities in the contract.
Scheduling Agreement - unlike a contract which only contains an overall target quantity or value - a scheduling agreement also contains specific order quantities and delivery dates.

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- negative impact on the client service delivery levels/client satisfaction when delivery schemes are not adhered to and may lead to loss of customers or claims when non timely delivery causes damage.

MM-MD: Mass Maintain Material Master Data
riskText:
Material Master Data is key Master Data in SAP R/3 as it has links to Sales, Purchasing, Production Planning, Material Forecasting, Distribution and Invoicing.  Basically, businesses cannot utilize SAP R/3 without a properly configured Material Master and properly maintained Material Master Data.

E.g. when a material number is entered into a sales order.  SAP automatically transfers relative data like item category, delivering plant, cost, and export data directly into the sales order.  This eliminated user creation of this data, but also shows the importance of correct material master data.

Several different views of Material Master Data exist in SAP.
General/ Basic data view applies to all organizational levels and exists at client (Mandant) level and contains Material Number, Description, Unit of measure, Division, Technical Data, Language,
Purchasing data view applies to Plant level and contains Purchasing group, Base unit of measure, MRP Type, Planned delivery time, Batch Indicator, Profit Center, 
Finance and Controlling view applies to Plant level and contains Price Control, Account Group, Standard Price, Moving Average Price, Pricing Unit
Other views refer to Sales Organizations, Storage Locations and Batch information

Some important/relevant Material Master Fields
The automatic PO indicator specifies that purchase orders are generated automatically
when requisitions are converted
The purchasing value key specifies the value key to be used for the default values for various fields for purchase orders raised against the material - including over-delivery tolerances
The source list indicator specifies that the source list must have been maintained in the case of external procurement for a certain plant 
Quality Inspection specifies whether the material is subject to quality inspection, and whether a goods receipt is posted to stock in quality inspection 
Item Category group Indicator in the sales organization screen triggers the item
category in a sales document and the schedule line category
Material statistics group key indicator triggers tracking in the Sales Information System
Standard, Moving Average & Price Control Fields trigger for all Material Movements whether Standard or Moving Average Price as the unit price times quantity for the movement value will be used 
Relevant for costing indicator specifies whether the material is subject to automated system generated pricing

Proper control of standard prices is crucial in any system but even more in SAP as all material movements are posted at the standard (std) or moving average price (mva) in the material master.  The difference between std and mva is determined by the price control field in the accounting screen of the material master.  Many organizations use mva pricing for raw materials as it reflects the average price of all activity for that material.  This allows them to use the cost that’s closest to actual for production.
Moving average pricing for finished goods could create differences in price between production plants and external shipping points.  Any differences in stock transfer between plants could cause unnecessary variances being posted, which are direct differences to the P & L financial statement.

The creation of material master should be restricted to a limited number of users. The integrity of all transactional data and reporting, depends on the quality of the material master data.

description: MM: Maintain Vendor Master Data Account group

riskText:
Vendor Master data is stored at three levels:
1.  General data applies to every company code and every purchasing organization. The general area includes, for example, the vendor's name, address, language, and telephone number.
2.  Company code data that is specific to an individual company code. Company code data includes, for example, reconciliation account number and payment terms.
3.  Purchasing organization data specific to purchasing organizations and relevant to raising requests for quotations, purchase orders etc.  For example - conditions, minimum order value.. 

Separate transactions and authorizations are available to segregate maintenance of Company Code (Accounting) and Purchasing data.  They can also be maintained centrally using a single transaction.

Each vendor must be assigned to an account group.  This then determines the account number assignment and screen layouts.

One-time vendor accounts are used for vendors from whom goods are expected only to be procured once or very rarely.
Where one-time vendors are required, a separate account group is normally established in conjunction with a one-time vendor master record.  The initial screen for the account group includes a flag to specify that the group is for one-time accounts. Since address and bank account details are entered during invoice/order entry a normal segregation of duties does not operate and compensating controls need to be considered.  These might include:
- Exception reporting of one-time vendor transactions to facilitate independent review
- Use of blocking flags to enforce independent release for payment

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:
- increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy suppliers customers, …
- sub-optimal use or loss of purchasing power

Company code data is for financial accounting information. (like reconciliation account, payment terms, payment method,..)

From a financial viewpoint, there are two levels of a customer master record:
General data that is entered once for a client (i.e., address, bank details)
Company code data  (i.e., reconciliation account) can vary for each company code.  
  Examples of company code data are: Payment transactions, Dunning, Correspondence, Interest calculation,...

If a customer is maintained centrally (at the client level), there is a third level containing Sales information.
In the Sales and Distribution module, a customer’s sales, billing, and shipping information can be recorded. (see query: VCUSTA - XCUSTA)

Unauthorized or inappropriate changes to these master data can have consequences like:

  - increased vulnerability to fraud, creation of dummy customers, ...
